samples.summary: `assertNoDotSegments` re-implements `seg()`'s refusal (including a hand-copied `Invalid path segment: "..."` message string) instead of reusing a helper exported from `client/url.ts`. The whole point of extracting `url.ts` was that the rule lives in one place; the dry-run printer now owns a second copy that can drift from the first (e.g. if `seg()` ever refuses more than `.`/`..`, or its message changes).
samples.evidence: dry-run.ts:43-51 duplicates url.ts:24-28's dot check and error text.

samples.summary: The one-segment invariant is enforced by convention at ~20 call sites rather than structurally. `printDryRun` takes an already-assembled `path` string and only re-checks for bare `.`/`..`; a command that forgets `seg()` on an id containing `/` but no dot segment (e.g. `other-ws/api-keys/k`) would still print a walked-out URL as "the request that would be sent", which is precisely the failure the design doc §10 says the preview must not have. An API that took id segments (or ids + a path template) would make the property unforgeable instead of remembered.
samples.evidence: printDryRun(config, method, path, body) with assertNoDotSegments(path) as the only check; every caller in commands/*.ts must remember to wrap each id in seg().

samples.summary: Dry-run request previews are built in four places — `client/dry-run.ts` plus hand-rolled `{method, path, body}` JSON in `docs/import.ts`, `notes/import.ts` and `slides/import.ts` — and this change perpetuates that by only sprinkling `seg()` into the copies rather than routing them through `printDryRun`. The updated design doc (§10) describes the preview as "a second URL builder (`printDryRun`)", which understates the actual duplication; these three copies emit no `url`, no workspace and no dry-run flag, so the preview an agent reads differs by command.
samples.evidence: docs/import.ts:156-165, notes/import.ts:145-155, slides/import.ts:181-190 each JSON.stringify their own preview shape.

samples.summary: The §10 matrix edit goes beyond documenting `HTTP_ERROR` (the stated acceptance criterion): it deletes the published `UNAUTHORIZED` and `SYSTEM` codes, rewrites the 401/403 and 5xx exit codes from 2 to 1, and adds a '† Planned, not shipped' annotation to the Yorkie/fontkit rows. The rewrite matches the shipped code (no path in packages/cli/src sets exit 2 or those codes, verified by grep), so it is corrective rather than wrong — but retiring two documented agent-facing codes is a contract change the todo did not ask for, and it is worth an explicit call-out in the PR description rather than riding along in an error-forwarding change.
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §10 rows for 'Backend 401/403' and 'Backend 5xx' replaced; §8.1 exit-code sentence rewritten.

searchedFor: grep for /documents/${ and workspaces/${ across packages/cli/src
finding.summary: New doc claims dot-segment ids are always refused and that ids are always one segment, but the `--dry-run` path bypasses `seg()` entirely
finding.evidence: The delta adds to docs/design/cli.md an unconditional error-matrix row — "Workspace / document / tab / cell id is `.` or `..` | 1 | ERROR | ... (refused before any request is sent)" — and prose that "Every id the client interpolates into a request URL ... is percent-encoded". The dry-run preview, which §8.2 defines as "prints the request that would be sent", builds its URL independently in `printDryRun` (`${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}`) from raw, unencoded ids supplied by the command layer (e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:55, docs.ts:188, notes.ts:140). So `wafflebase docs content '..' --dry-run` exits 0 and prints a traversing URL rather than the documented ERROR/exit 1, and the previewed URL does not match the URL the real call would send for any id needing encoding. Either the doc row needs a dry-run carve-out or `printDryRun` should share the same segment encoding.

verdict.reason: The claimed code does not exist as described. `printDryRun` (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:20-41) calls `assertNoDotSegments(path)` and builds the URL with `seg(config.workspace)`, not raw ids; `assertNoDotSegments` (dry-run.ts:43-52) throws the same `Invalid path segment` error `seg()` raises (url.ts:24-28). The three command-layer lines the reviewer cites as supplying raw ids all wrap them in `seg()`: cells.ts:56, docs.ts:191, notes.ts:146 — as do every other dry-run path (tabs.ts:52,81; files.ts:64,124,144; slides.ts:100,120,152,203; sheets-import.ts:88; docs.ts:135,155,246; notes.ts:95,115,201). Therefore `docs content '..' --dry-run` throws from `seg(docId)` inside the command's try block (docs.ts:184-192) rather than exiting 0 with a traversing URL, and the previewed URL is encoded identically to the real request. The design doc also already carves the dry-run path in explicitly (docs/design/cli.md:1107-1113), so there is no doc/implementation mismatch to fix.
